name: Baptisia

project_scope.note: Genus lesson structurally live; species taxonomy/range installation remains species-lane work and is not promoted by this module.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Start with the herbaceous habit and trifoliolate leaves: three leaflets arise together, unlike the palmate many-leaflet Lupinus pattern. Then confirm pea-family flowers and an inflated to ovoid legume pod.
recognition.local_anchor: Baptisia bracteata — source concept for the current project pool; genus-level teaching anchor only until species-lane taxonomy/range review is durably resolved.

comparisons.rule: Baptisia commonly has three leaflets per leaf; Lupinus texensis has a conspicuously palmately compound leaf with several narrow leaflets radiating from one point.
Baptisia is herbaceous with trifoliolate leaves; Dermatophyllum secundiflorum is a woody evergreen with glossy pinnate leaves.
Use the one-carpel legume fruit plus stipules and pea-flower architecture to confirm family placement; do not identify Baptisia from flower color alone.

visual_needs: whole flowering plant showing herbaceous architecture
single trifoliolate leaf with attachment and stipules visible
